citation: Ngo, Dehesa-Azuara, Fredrikson & Hoffmann, Verifying and Synthesizing Constant-Resource Implementations with Types, IEEE S&P 2017
what_primary_source_supports: AARA is combined with information-flow tracking to establish resource-aware noninterference; the attacker observes modeled resource consumption.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Directly defeats novelty claims for the general combination of IFC and resource security. Its semantics use an explicit cost model; it does not study provider-mediated LLM billing.

citation: Çiçek, Barthe, Gaboardi, Garg & Hoffmann, Relational Cost Analysis, POPL 2017
what_primary_source_supports: Relational refinement analysis bounds differences between execution costs and reasons across related executions.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Foundational relational-cost method. It does not establish an OrchLang-specific model/request coupling or provider billing trace.

citation: Radiček, Barthe, Gaboardi, Garg & Zuleger, Monadic Refinements for Relational Cost Analysis, POPL 2018
what_primary_source_supports: A compositional refinement and cost-monad system combines relational cost reasoning with functional properties.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Further evidence that compositional relational cost reasoning is established. Does not analyze opaque model API calls or invoices.

citation: Ngo, Carbonneaux & Hoffmann, Bounded Expectations: Resource Analysis for Probabilistic Programs, PLDI 2018
what_primary_source_supports: Static analysis derives upper bounds on expected resource consumption of probabilistic programs.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Refutes categorical claims that numerical resource analysis cannot apply to stochastic programs. Expected bounds are not pathwise billing-trace noninterference.

citation: Mandel, Baudart, Vaziri & Hirzel, PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs, ICML 2026, PMLR 306:86172–86197
what_primary_source_supports: A probabilistic language for multi-call LLM/tool flow traces and output distributions; the full paper evaluates inference strategies under total-token budgets and logs token usage in a proof-repair case study.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Material recent counterexample to claims that LLM workflows have no probabilistic semantics, trace distributions, token budgets, or usage logging. It does not claim a static secret-conditioned usage-observer leakage bound or equality of billing traces under a request/history coupling.

citation: Köpf & Basin, An Information-Theoretic Model for Adaptive Side-Channel Attacks, CCS 2007
what_primary_source_supports: Models adaptive side-channel observations and quantifies remaining attacker uncertainty.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Supports quantitative leakage framing and attacker-observation precision. It is not a source-level checker for model billing traces.

citation: Beurer-Kellner, Fischer & Vechev, Prompting Is Programming: A Query Language for Large Language Models, PLDI 2023 (PACMPL)
what_primary_source_supports: Presents a prompt/query language with output constraints and interaction with external tools.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Counters novelty claims about adding a programming language or structured constraints for LLM prompts; not a token-billing noninterference analysis.

citation: Dong et al., APPL: A Prompt Programming Language for Harmonious Integration of Programs and Large Language Model Prompts, ACL 2025
what_primary_source_supports: Python-native prompt programming, asynchronous/parallel runtime, tracing/replay, and representative CoT self-consistency and ReAct examples.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Relevant language/runtime baseline and source for workflow patterns. No static information-flow or billing-trace theorem is claimed by the cited paper.

citation: Vaziri et al., PDL: A Declarative Prompt Programming Language, arXiv:2410.19135
publication_status: Preprint; no peer-reviewed venue located in this targeted check
what_primary_source_supports: Declarative prompt/workflow representation with tools, control flow, loops and functions; primary arXiv record and linked project repository.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Useful language comparison and source examples. Cite as a preprint, not as a peer-reviewed result; no billing-trace noninterference claim.

citation: Debenedetti et al., Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL), arXiv:2503.18813 v2
what_primary_source_supports: Separates trusted-query control/data flow and uses capabilities to mediate tool flows; reports results on AgentDojo.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Strong neighboring defense: OrchLang must state its own static source-level property and not imply prompt-injection robustness. CaMeL's paper is not a token-billing analysis.

citation: Costa et al., Securing AI Agents with Information-Flow Control (FIDES), arXiv:2505.23643 v2
what_primary_source_supports: Formalizes agent planner properties, characterizes dynamic taint enforceability, and presents confidentiality/integrity label tracking and selective hiding.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Close agent-IFC work. The cited version is a preprint; its focus is runtime planner policy and task utility, not exact model/request billing trace.

citation: Shivakumar, Priya & Gao, AgentFlow: A Flow-Centric Policy Language and Framework for Securing LLM Agent Systems, arXiv:2608.22868 v1
what_primary_source_supports: Describes a flow policy language, runtime reference monitor, and bounded SMT verifier for a structured policy subset; results are explicitly preliminary and scoped to evaluated behavior.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Counters 'agent security is runtime-only' and 'no static workflow verification.' It addresses policy-visible data flow, not equal billing under a shared model oracle.

citation: Xavier et al., Agentproof: Static Verification of Agent Workflow Graphs, arXiv:2603.20356 v1
what_primary_source_supports: Extracts abstract graphs from four agent frameworks and checks graph structure and DFA-compiled temporal policies statically and at runtime; uses an author-constructed 18-workflow benchmark.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Counters 'static verification of agent workflows does not exist.' The paper's properties concern graph topology/temporal policy, not request identity or billing. Its benchmark is not a prevalence sample.

citation: Ghost in the Agent: Redefining Information Flow Tracking for LLM Agents, arXiv:2604.23374 v1
what_primary_source_supports: Describes offline trace auditing/provenance reconstruction for agent information flows.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Different lifecycle point: post-hoc audit is neither compile-time enforcement nor a billing-trace equality proof. Verify author/version metadata before final citation.

citation: Khan, Token Budgets: An Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents, with an Affine-Typed Rust Mitigation as a Case Study, arXiv:2606.04056 v1
what_primary_source_supports: Reports an author-assembled incident catalog and a Rust affine budget type/runtime enforcement case study.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Adjacent token-budget engineering. It does not show those incidents are representative or prove secret-independent cost; its estimated reservation slack is not comparable to OrchLang's synthetic corpus ratios.

citation: Weiss et al., What Was Your Prompt? A Remote Keylogging Attack on AI Assistants, USENIX Security 2024
what_primary_source_supports: Demonstrates inference of prompt content from encrypted traffic using token-length side-channel observations.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Evidence that token-length observables can be security-relevant. It is a network-traffic attack, not evidence about provider invoices or OrchLang's exact property.

citation: Zhang et al., Time Will Tell: Timing Side Channels via Output Token Count in Large Language Models, arXiv:2412.15431
publication_status: Preprint; no peer-reviewed venue located in this targeted check
what_primary_source_supports: Studies remote latency as a side channel correlated with output token count and secret attributes.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Supports latency as a distinct possible observable. Do not present as peer-reviewed or as a billing attack; timing is outside OrchLang's current observation model.

citation: Early Bird Catches the Leak: Unveiling Timing Side Channels in LLM Serving Systems, arXiv:2409.20002
publication_status: Preprint; venue status not verified in this audit
what_primary_source_supports: Studies timing leakage in LLM serving systems, including cache/prefix effects as described in its primary abstract.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Optional adjacent side-channel source. Verify publication status before describing it as peer-reviewed; it does not prove invoice disclosure.

citation: Dickerson, Statically Bounding Resource Accumulation in LLM Agent Workflows: The Cost Case (18 May 2026)
publication_status: Author-hosted research note; no peer-reviewed venue or DOI located in targeted check
what_primary_source_supports: The author states a structural Petri-net analyzer for upper-bounding cumulative monotone resources, develops token cost as a corollary, and reports 25 live-model parameter combinations without observed bound violations.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Direct neighboring unary cumulative-resource analysis for LLM-agent workflows. Treat its status and empirical claims as author-reported, not peer-reviewed or independently reproduced. It does not establish two-run usage equality under a shared request-sensitive oracle.

citation: Barthe, D'Argenio & Rezk, Secure Information Flow by Self-Composition, IEEE CSFW 2004
what_primary_source_supports: Introduces self-composition as a way to reduce relational secure-information-flow reasoning to verification of a composed program.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Foundational prior art for the two-execution/product construction. It is not an OrchLang-specific external-call or usage-trace analysis.

citation: Barthe, Crespo & Kunz, Product Programs and Relational Program Logics, Journal of Logical and Algebraic Methods in Programming 85(5), 2016
what_primary_source_supports: Compares product-program and relational-logic approaches for 2-safety, including noninterference, and discusses loop synchronization and program alignment.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Direct prior art for paired-state products and relational control alignment. An OrchLang graph checker that reuses this construction for abstract model-call descriptors is an application, not a new product-program or bisimulation theory.

citation: Barthe, Espitau, Grégoire, Hsu, Stefanesco & Strub, Relational Reasoning via Probabilistic Coupling, LPAR 2015
what_primary_source_supports: Defines a coupling as a joint distribution with the two target distributions as marginals; relational program logic uses coupling witnesses to establish relations between probabilistic executions and distributions.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Directly supports the conditional distributional corollary: a coupling supported on equal usage traces implies equal marginal usage-trace laws. It is standard prior art and does not validate any LLM provider kernel.

citation: Barthe & Hsu, Probabilistic Couplings from Program Logics, Foundations of Probabilistic Programming, Cambridge University Press 2020, pp. 145–184
what_primary_source_supports: Explains that couplings preserve specified marginals and establish relational properties of probabilistic programs; discusses probabilistic bisimulation and compositional coupling proofs.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Primary explanatory source for the coupling argument and its limits. The OrchLang stochastic-kernel corollary is a direct application, not a novel coupling method or empirical provider result.

citation: Chothia, Kawamoto, Novakovic & Parker, Probabilistic Point-to-Point Information Leakage, IEEE CSF 2013
what_primary_source_supports: Defines a quantitative leakage model between arbitrary points in probabilistic imperative programs, including nontermination and user input, and reports a tool/approximation study.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Direct prior art for localizing and quantifying probabilistic leakage. A finite LLM-workflow usage-trace analysis would be a domain-specific semantics/implementation contribution, not a new point-to-point leakage model.

citation: Schröer, Randone, Pardo & Wąsowski, Symbolic Quantitative Information Flow for Probabilistic Programs, Principles of Verification, LNCS 15260, 2024
what_primary_source_supports: Computes symbolic entropy, conditional entropy, KL divergence, and mutual information; for discrete probabilistic programs it uses weakest pre-expectations to obtain exact symbolic expressions, while its mixed continuous setting uses Gaussian approximation/bounds.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Rules out claims that exact symbolic MI or probabilistic QIF metrics are themselves new. A proposed usage-channel analyzer would need a precise workflow-specific composition theorem and demonstrated precision/utility.

citation: Anjum et al., ProMCP: Profiling Token Flows and Latency Costs in Model Context Protocol–Based LLM Agents, Findings of ACL 2026
what_primary_source_supports: Profiles a six-stage MCP host/client/server communication pipeline and measures token and latency attribution across 20 servers and 169 tools.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Directly adjacent workflow-cost instrumentation. It profiles observed runs rather than proving source-level confidentiality or equal billing traces; it makes broad 'no workflow token-cost tool exists' claims untenable.

citation: Sun et al., Position: Invisible Tokens, Visible Bills: The Urgent Need to Audit Hidden Operations in Opaque LLM Services, ICML 2026, PMLR 306:172196–172207
what_primary_source_supports: Frames quantity inflation and quality downgrade in commercial opaque LLM services and discusses commitment-, predictive-, behavioral-, and signature-based audit strategies.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Motivates billing accountability but concerns provider-side hidden operations and auditability. OrchLang neither attests provider execution nor verifies invoices.

citation: Guo et al., IMMACULATE: A Practical LLM Auditing Framework via Verifiable Computation, arXiv:2602.22700
what_primary_source_supports: Proposes selective verifiable-computation audits to detect execution deviations including model substitution, quantization abuse, and token overbilling without trusted hardware or model internals; the abstract reports experiments on dense and MoE models.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Strong adjacent provider-execution/billing audit. It is an arXiv preprint as of this audit. It targets execution/report integrity, not source-level secret-dependent usage-trace equality.

citation: Hoque, Zhang, Sun & Suya, Token Inflation: How Dishonest Providers Can Overcharge for Large Language Model Usage, arXiv:2605.30040
what_primary_source_supports: Studies provider token-count overreporting and the audit trust problem when verification evidence is controlled by the audited provider; the abstract reports tokenization ambiguity and hidden-reasoning scenarios.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Makes clear that a compiler-side abstract cost proof is not an invoice or provider-report audit. The authors' experimental claims remain preprint claims, not independently replicated here.

citation: Zhang et al., Persistent Billable State: Denial-of-Wallet Attacks and Defenses in Tool-Calling LLM Agents, arXiv:2609.28585
what_primary_source_supports: Studies how retained tool returns re-enter later billable prompts, derives denial-of-wallet vectors, evaluates history policies, and proposes host-side bounds before reingestion.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Close to multi-call cumulative usage and stateful workflows, but addresses host-controlled billable context and cost growth rather than secret-dependent trace equality. Author-reported results are not treated as independently verified.

citation: Chen et al., The More It Says, the More You Pay: A Black-Box Audit of Provider-Side Token Inflation in LLM Services, arXiv:2609.20370
what_primary_source_supports: Proposes black-box probes for provider-side output-token inflation; the abstract reports experiments on four open models and 15 API services.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Adjacent provider audit and useful motivation, but does not verify static workflow semantics or prove a privacy guarantee. Reported service detections are preliminary author claims from a preprint.

citation: IBM, Prompt Declaration Language tutorial: Accessing the pdl_usage variable
what_primary_source_supports: Documents runtime counters for model calls, prompt tokens, completion tokens, and total token usage, with a usage example inside a PDL flow.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Confirms that workflow token-usage collection is already available in an adjacent framework. Runtime counters do not calculate a secret-conditioned usage channel or establish a static relational confidentiality property.

citation: Larsen & Skou, Bisimulation through Probabilistic Testing, Information and Computation 94(1), 1991, pp. 1–28
what_primary_source_supports: Defines probabilistic bisimulation over probabilistic transition systems and develops a testing characterization.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Foundational prior art for exact strong probabilistic partition refinement. OrchLang specializes this method to finite request/history states and visible usage labels; it does not introduce new bisimulation theory.

citation: Kamaleson, Parker & Rowe, Finite-Horizon Bisimulation Minimisation for Probabilistic Systems, SPIN 2016, LNCS 9641, pp. 147–164
what_primary_source_supports: Formalizes finite-horizon probabilistic bisimulation and gives partition-refinement and on-the-fly minimization algorithms for probabilistic systems.
boundary_for_OrchLang: Shows finite-horizon probabilistic bisimulation minimization is established model-checking practice. OrchLang's all-horizon fixed-point checker is a workflow-specific application and only proves a sufficient trace-law equality relation.
